Definition: probably akin to the base of G58 (through the idea of collecting one's faculties); to waken (transitively or intransitively), i.e. rouse (literally, from sleep, from sitting or lying, from disease, from death; or figuratively, from obscurity, inactivity, ruins, nonexistence):--awake, lift (up), raise (again, up), rear up, (a-)rise (again, up), stand, take up.
BiblicalUsage: To raise is to wake from sleep, to stand up from lying down, and to rise from the dead, and the New Testament uses one word for all three. The angel says He is not here, for He is risen, the women find the tomb empty on the first day, and Paul says Christ was buried and rose again the third day according to the Scriptures. The same word that wakes a sleeper raises a Saviour, and it will raise us too.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the resurrection is the hinge of my faith, because if Christ is not raised, my preaching and my hope are empty. He is risen, and that means death is not the end of my story either.
